tools.name: list_supported_sites
tools.description:
List the sites FetchPan can download from, with live status (working, slow, down).

        `main_sites` are the big ones (Baidu, Quark, Rapidgator ...). `file_hosts` are the other
        file hosts. `free` tells whether a free download is possible there or only a paid one.

tools.name: check_link
tools.description:
Is this link from a site FetchPan supports, and is that site working right now?

        Does not use any quota. Call it before `download` when you are not sure.

tools.name: start_download
tools.description: Start fetching a link. Returns a job id; poll it with `get_job`. Uses no free file yet.

tools.name: get_job
tools.description:
Status of a job: queued, running, succeeded or failed.

        When it has succeeded it also says whether a free download is possible (`free`) and what a
        fast one would cost in traffic bytes (`fast`).

tools.name: get_download_link
tools.description:
Get the download URL of a succeeded job. A free link uses one of the account's free
        files for the day; a fast link uses traffic from the account balance. Asking again for the
        same job and tier returns the same link.

tools.name: download
tools.description:
Fetch a link and return a download URL, in one call.

        Waits up to `wait_seconds` for the file to be ready. If it is not ready yet, the result has
        status "running" and a `job_id`: call `get_job`, then `get_download_link`.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description:
The account behind the token: email, traffic balance in bytes, free files per day,
        and the last downloads.

tools.name: list_packages
tools.description: Traffic packs that can be bought (code, size in bytes, price in USDT).

tools.name: create_payment_link
tools.description:
Create a payment page for a traffic pack and return its URL. Give the URL to the
        user: only a person can pay it. Nothing is charged by calling this.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_download_link, download, get_account · Private data: list_supported_sites, start_download, get_download_link, download, get_account · Public sink: get_account.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_download_link, download, get_account · Private data: list_supported_sites, start_download, get_download_link, download, get_account · Public sink: get_account

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
